properties.description: The alleged 25 January 2000 SS647 bridge failure near Campobasso is not established by the supplied audit. The inaccessible Sudnews reference carries a recorded publication date in January 2001, while a separate major flood affected the Biferno basin in January 2003. Bridge identity, event year and physical failure extent remain unresolved. The existing date remains an unverified historical attribution, not a confirmed fact. The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated.

The October 2000 report describes an irreparably damaged stone-arch bridge in central Crissolo, a provisional crossing with eroded accesses and other upstream damaged/destroyed crossings. The bridge corresponding to this record has not been uniquely matched. The existing beam / reinforced-concrete fields remain provisional; stone-arch coding is conditional on identifying the historic central crossing. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. The PC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated.

A second Crissolo crossing is attributed to supplementary case P008, with bank/embankment erosion and reported abutment/deck damage. The supplied audit did not inspect that record or uniquely identify the crossing. Eroded approaches alone do not establish PC. The two Crissolo records remain separate pending proof of distinct structures. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P008, classifies the process as lateral bank/embankment erosion with damage involving abutment/superstructure components. The official ARPA Piemonte report independently documents severe bridge damage and destroyed crossings along the Po in the Crissolo area. The PC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P008, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The regional report documents destruction of a pedestrian crossing at Cresto in Ala di Stura through lateral erosion and loss of support. This supports a physical TC at Cresto, but the match to this record’s coordinates and original structural/material fields remains unresolved. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed.

Several crossings in Ala di Stura were affected: La Fabbrica was partly destroyed by erosion, the SP1 bridge over Rio Molar was damaged and a separate municipal crossing at Pian del Tetto was affected by Rio Ruè. The specific provincial crossing represented here remains unidentified. The detailed process is unverified. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. The PC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated.

The regional report explicitly records collapse of Ponte delle Scale following Stura erosion. Matching this documented municipal crossing to the present record’s coordinates is still required. No replacement or guessed structural characteristics are assigned. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', IJDRR, database supplementare S3, record P017 (dec=1, ciclopedonale, crollo totale, coordinate coincidenti con la scheda): processo = carico idraulico sulla struttura; componente = impalcato. La scheda indica tipologia 'Municipal': discrepanza tipologica da verificare (Ala di Stura, piena dello Stura, ott. 2000). The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P017, codes hydraulic load. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity. Hydraulic load is not synonymous with observed overtopping (S3 overtopping: ?).

The 1935 SP41 bridge between Feletto and Lusigliè over the Orco failed during the October 2000 flood. The regional report describes foundation scour and settlement of the central pier followed by failure of the bridge structure. The municipality spelling is corrected to Feletto; TC is retained. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Rapporto d'evento Regione Piemonte - Direzione Servizi Tecnici di Prevenzione (aprile 2001): nel corso della piena dell'Orco l'erosione di fondo ha provocato il sottoscalzamento della pila centrale e il cedimento dell'intera struttura del ponte SP41 tra Feletto e Lusiglie' (edificato nel 1935). S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P003, codes vertical erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The historic Ponte Pietra Bogone in Balme was completely destroyed during the October 2000 flood. Its correspondence to this first Balme record still requires coordinate matching. The bridge name alone does not establish its original structural type or material. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed.

A separate bridge serving Villa Sigismondi at Balme collapsed after erosion of the right abutment and left approach embankment. Another pedestrian crossing over Rio Paschiet was swept away. Matching this second Balme record to the correct crossing is required before finalizing identity and independence. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed.

The official report documents destruction and damage to several crossings in Chialamberto, but does not independently identify the precise pedestrian bridge represented by this record. Bridge-specific physical failure has not been independently established. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated.

Severe erosion and damage affected crossings and access roads in Chialamberto. A provincial bridge on the Stura di Valgrande may correspond to this record, but the actual bridge and physical span failure remain unresolved. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed.

Road crossings around Miradolo and Pinerolo were affected by flooding and loss of access. Inundation or an impassable approach does not by itself establish complete structural collapse. The specific road bridge represented here remains unresolved. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Monografia 'Eventi alluvionali in Piemonte 2000-2002' (Regione Piemonte/ARPA, 2003): i ponti affiancati (stradale e ferroviario) di via Saluzzo a Pinerolo furono entrambi danneggiati in modo irreparabile; il restringimento d'alveo da essi causato costitui' un significativo ostacolo al deflusso, concorrendo alla sommersione della zona Ponte Chisone. Meccanismo di dettaglio del manufatto stradale non specificato. The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated.

The regional report describes damage to a Chisone crossing involving right-pier settlement and left-abutment erosion, and separately loss of the left abutment of Ponte Miradolo. These are primary-support failures, but the exact crossing corresponding to this second Pinerolo record still needs identification. PC is retained by curator decision. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Monografia 'Eventi alluvionali in Piemonte 2000-2002' (Regione Piemonte/ARPA, 2003): asportata la spalla sinistra del ponte di Miradolo sul Chisone; il ponte, di antico impianto, risulta tra quelli distrutti dall'evento. Conferma quanto gia' indicato dal rapporto d'evento 2001. The PC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P032, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The regional report identifies collapse of the railway bridge at Ponte San Martino along the Chisone and associates failure with intense riverbed erosion. TC is retained; the original span arrangement and steel versus reinforced-concrete configuration require verification independently of replacement bridges. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Rapporto d'evento 2001: abbattuto il ponte ferroviario Pinerolo-Torre Pellice a via Saluzzo (piena del Chisone); un passaggio attiguo attribuisce i danni 'soprattutto a erosioni lungo il fondo alveo' con 'cedimento della pila di destra per erosione di fondo' (attribuzione probabile per impaginazione). Monografia 'Eventi alluvionali in Piemonte 2000-2002' (Regione Piemonte/ARPA, 2003): conferma che il ponte ferroviario di via Saluzzo fu danneggiato in modo irreparabile, in coppia con l'attiguo ponte stradale, il cui restringimento d'alveo ostacolo' il deflusso.

Flood-related bridge/support damage is documented in the Sangone basin, but the supplied audit does not uniquely identify the Giaveno crossing represented by this record. TC is retained by curator decision. Earlier specific Master attributions are retained below for reconciliation rather than silently discarded. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Monografia 'Eventi alluvionali in Piemonte 2000-2002' (Regione Piemonte/ARPA, 2003): crollato alle ore 18:00 del 15/10 il ponte della SP193 Giaveno-Cumiana sul Sangone: cedettero 2 pile in corrispondenza del notevole ampliamento d'alveo in sinistra idrografica, in un tratto pluricanale a marcata instabilita' con abbondante trasporto solido. The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P022, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The Orco flood caused severe erosion near SS460 and other road connections around Castellamonte. Exact bridge identity and whether damage affected primary span members rather than an embankment remain unresolved in this audit. The existing one-fatality attribution is retained but must be tied to the correct crossing and chronology. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Monografia 'Eventi alluvionali in Piemonte 2000-2002' (Regione Piemonte/ARPA, 2003): l'accentuata erosione dei terreni in sinistra dell'Orco convoglio' le acque contro la parte in rilevato del ponte della SS 'Pedemontana' a Castellamonte, portandone alla distruzione (crollo parziale la mattina di domenica 15/10, con una vittima successiva). Nota: la monografia scrive S.S.656, il rapporto 2001 S.S.565, il DB S.S.460: uniformare la denominazione.

A pier of the central municipal bridge at Noasca failed on the morning of 17 October 2000 after the bridge had been closed. The present record has not been matched conclusively to that structure. The stored 13 October date is not automatically replaced and the documented 17 October failure is not assigned to both Noasca records. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Monografia 'Eventi alluvionali in Piemonte 2000-2002' (Regione Piemonte/ARPA, 2003): al 'nodo di Noasca' intensi processi di mobilizzazione del fondo alveo con forte restringimento dell'alveo danneggiarono gravemente passerella e opere di difesa; il rapporto 2001 documenta inoltre violenti processi di erosione laterale e di fondo con gravi danni alle opere di attraversamento. Meccanismo del singolo ponte non distinto.

The Robassomero–Ciriè provincial crossing over the Stura di Lanzo suffered right-bank erosion, loss of support and collapse of a deck section during the October flood. The road became impassable. TC is retained, with the precise extent of the failed primary span system still to be documented. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Rapporto d'evento Regione Piemonte - Direzione Servizi Tecnici di Prevenzione (aprile 2001): 'Crollo del ponte sullo Stura della SP Robassomero-Cirie' per erosione in sponda destra', con crollo di un tratto dell'impalcato; a valle la stessa erosione ha messo a giorno le fondazioni di un capannone e danneggiato la centrale elettrica. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P002, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The Salassa record is linked to supplementary case P004, which attributes lateral erosion and damage to multiple bridge/access components. The supplied audit did not inspect the supplementary case or uniquely identify the original bridge. Multiple damaged components alone do not establish TC. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P004 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = pile, spalle, rilevato di accesso, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no. The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P004, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

Collapse of the railway bridge near Settimo Vittone on the connection towards Valle d’Aosta is historically documented for the October 2000 flood. TC is retained. Steel-truss coding and the original span configuration remain provisional pending original structural documentation. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Rapporto d'evento Regione Piemonte - Direzione Servizi Tecnici di Prevenzione (aprile 2001): asportato il ponte ferroviario della linea Torino-Aosta a Settimo Vittone durante l'esondazione della Dora Baltea, che ha sovrappassato la SS26 per ~1 km. [Il database Polimi (D'Angelo et al. 2025, S3, record P005, dec=1) classifica invece il processo come: erosione laterale di sponda.] S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P005, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The upper Po flood severely damaged crossings near Paesana. The specific bridge represented here has not been independently identified. Bank erosion and abutment damage do not by themselves establish complete-span collapse. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Rapporto d'evento Regione Piemonte - Direzione Servizi Tecnici di Prevenzione (aprile 2001): l'erosione del Po in loc. Erasca ha asportato l'accesso al ponte in sponda sinistra e la spalla sinistra del ponte. The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P009, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The Bardonecchia bridge record remains unresolved. The recorded hydronym “Bora di Bardonecchia” requires checking against the exact watercourse; the crossing could instead be on a tributary. The name is not automatically replaced by Dora di Bardonecchia or Dora di Rochemolles without identifying the bridge. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Rapporto d'evento Regione Piemonte - Direzione Servizi Tecnici di Prevenzione (aprile 2001): per Bardonecchia il rapporto documenta un solo ponte gravemente colpito: 'erosioni di sponda e di fondo con asportazione della pila del ponte per Millaures e di parte del rilevato di accesso' (Dora di Rochemolles). Corrispondenza con la scheda (ponte nazionale su Dora di Bardonecchia) da verificare. The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated.

During the 13–16 October flood the bridge on the road to La Balma upstream of Roncaglie was swept away with adjacent municipal road infrastructure, in the Rio delle Boine episode at Bussoleno. The plotted point is a locality reference, not a verified bridge centroid. The exact failure day, original configuration and casualties remain unknown. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 13 October 2000 – 16 October 2000; the stored date 2000-10-13 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day.

properties.bridge_name: Passerella presso Combe sul Rio Gerardo
properties.description: The October flood swept away a pedestrian crossing near Combe on Rio Gerardo in the Bussoleno–Mattie area. The recorded point refers to the hamlet, not the bridge centroid; Mattie remains subject to final boundary/crossing confirmation. Original structural type and material are unknown. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed.

The regional report describes destruction of the bridge serving Inverso in Chialamberto during the October flood. The same process destroyed buildings and the principal valley water pipeline. A local/municipal crossing is documented, but the match to this third Chialamberto record requires coordinate reconciliation. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Monografia 'Eventi alluvionali in Piemonte 2000-2002' (Regione Piemonte/ARPA, 2003): a Chialamberto, loc. Inverso, lo Stura ampliando la propria sezione in destra idrografica asporto' totalmente le difese spondali, distrusse cinque edifici e 'il ponte di accesso alla localita'' con la condotta principale dell'acquedotto della valle. L'associazione a questa scheda (tra le tre di Chialamberto) e' probabile ma non certa. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P018, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The municipal/local road bridge serving San Colombano on Rio Galambra was completely removed, including its abutments, during the October flood. It belongs to the Exilles-area locality context, not an automatically accepted independent municipality. The National use classification is corrected to Municipal; municipality identity still requires geographical confirmation. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Rapporto d'evento Regione Piemonte - Direzione Servizi Tecnici di Prevenzione (aprile 2001): il ponte comunale sul rio Galambro per la frazione Colombano e' stato completamente asportato dalla piena, comprese le spalle; evidenti erosioni di fondo e materiale fluitato. (Il rapporto lo indica su strada comunale; il DB lo registra come nazionale: verificare.) S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P020, codes hydraulic load. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity. Hydraulic load is not synonymous with observed overtopping (S3 overtopping: yes).

Bank erosion affecting an abutment is attributed to the Fenestrelle record. The mechanism could be compatible with PC, but qualifying deformation of the supported primary structure has not been established for the exact crossing. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR, suppl. S3, record P021 (dec=0.5; abbinato per anno 2000 + coordinate, dist. 0.00 km): processo = erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = spalle; evidenza di sormonto = ?. [Nota QA precedente: il rapporto 2001 documenta a Fenestrelle danni al ponte del campeggio e lievi al ponte sul rio Gran Puy; la monografia 2003 il parziale scalzamento delle spalle del ponte per il Laux (Usseaux): corrispondenza puntuale con questa scheda da verificare.] The PC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P021, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

Bonzo is a locality name that must be assigned to its correct administrative municipality after geographical verification. Flood damage to crossings and access infrastructure is documented in the valley, but the specific bridge and complete-span failure remain unresolved. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Rapporto d'evento Regione Piemonte - Direzione Servizi Tecnici di Prevenzione (aprile 2001): l'erosione in sinistra dello Stura ha asportato strada di accesso e rampa del ponte di Bonzo; eroso il risvolto della spalla sinistra. Il ponte era gia' parzialmente crollato nell'evento del 1993. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P023, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The Locana pedestrian-crossing record is linked to D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), supplementary table S3 P024 (row 170): author-reported length 60 m and lateral erosion are accepted. ARCUS maps the latter to Bank erosion / embankment failure; S3 P024 is not cited as evidence of foundation scour. The regional report separately describes a road bridge destroyed near Locana–Devion and other affected crossings. Those road-bridge losses and bed-erosion observations are not transferred to the pedestrian record. The stored 13 October date is the conventional start of the flood episode, not a newly proven bridge-specific day. Existing PC is retained by curator decision. Exact local identity and affected primary members remain separate review questions; they do not reopen the accepted S3 length and hydraulic classification.

The 17 October central-pier failure must not be assigned to both records without proving distinct bridge identities. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. S3, record P027 (dec=1; abbinato per anno 2000 + coordinate, dist. 0.00 km): processo = erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = spalle, rilevato di accesso; evidenza di sormonto = no. The PC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P027, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The regional report explicitly describes complete destruction of Ponte Inverso, connecting Inverso Pinasca to the opposite bank of the Chisone. Failure is associated with riverbed/foundation erosion. TC is retained. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Rapporto d'evento Regione Piemonte - Direzione Servizi Tecnici di Prevenzione (aprile 2001): distruzione completa del ponte di collegamento con Inverso Pinasca per erosioni di fondo del Chisone (loc. Ponte Inverso). S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P029, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

Railway crossings in the Chisone valley suffered major flood damage, but this San Germano record was not matched independently to a photograph or railway chainage. Its distinction from Ponte San Martino at Pinerolo and its steel-truss configuration require verification. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR, suppl. S3, record P030 (dec=1; abbinato per anno 2000 + coordinate, dist. 0.00 km): processo = erosione verticale (scour) + erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = pile, rilevato di accesso, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P030, codes vertical erosion; lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity. Multiple cause flags are retained, with no inferred dominant process.

At the Pont Canavese railway crossing the official report documents erosion/removal of both approach embankments. This is not independent evidence of severe deformation of the bridge superstructure or piers. The documented approach-embankment collapse is eligible under the restricted ARCUS operational extension; it is not independent evidence of primary-member failure. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Previous Master source attribution retained for reconciliation (not newly independently verified): Monografia 'Eventi alluvionali in Piemonte 2000-2002' (Regione Piemonte/ARPA, 2003): a valle della confluenza con il Soana la piena dell'Orco danneggio' la linea ferroviaria (Canavesana) asportando sia in destra sia in sinistra i rilevati di accesso al ponte ferroviario di Pont Canavese. The PC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated. ARCUS scope decision (15 October 2026): documented physical collapse of an approach embankment directly connected to the bridge; the restricted operational extension applies. This is distinct from NYSDOT structural span collapse. The existing TC/PC code is retained as a curator decision; this scope assessment does not independently establish lane passability or validate its operational severity threshold. Other record-specific limitations remain. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P033, codes embankment erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

Severe hydraulic damage occurred near the municipal Pont Canavese crossing and adjacent water-diversion works. The inspected passage does not establish complete-span destruction of this bridge. Damage to nearby hydraulic works must be distinguished from primary bridge-member failure. The stored 13 October date marks the beginning of the regional flood; the bridge-specific failure day remains to be confirmed. Constructed in the early 1930s and partly rebuilt after wartime destruction, the crossing later received a temporary replacement in June 2003 and a permanent bridge inaugurated in December 2006. No casualties are recorded. Scour is strongly supported by the historical account but lacks a detailed original engineering investigation. This provincial crossing is distinct from the SS16 structure involved in April 2026. Curator-reviewed event date: 25 January 2003; earlier cracking on 24 January is not counted as a separate collapse.

ARCUS therefore retains the 2003 and 2005 entries as source-distinguished episodes at the same named crossing, not as two different bridges. The intervening works are reported by the newspaper, not independently verified from an as-built or acceptance document. Original structural system, material, failed component and precise point remain unverified; existing fields are retained pending that separate review. TC and zero bridge-specific casualties are retained by curator decision. Characteristics of the later three-span replacement are not assigned to this event.

properties.bridge_name: Ponte sul Fiume Sangro – SS16 Adriatica
properties.description: On 24 October 2004 three southern spans of the SS16 Adriatica bridge over the Sangro collapsed. The designers describe the old bridge as twelve masonry-and-concrete arches with nominal 29 m spans, corresponding to approximately 348 m by summation, not a separately surveyed overall length. The road bridge was built in 1949. The controlled Masonry label is retained with this mixed construction explicitly qualified; several concrete elements were weakly reinforced or unreinforced. Foundation scour initiated the failure, with material/foundation vulnerability and asymmetric thrust among the contributing factors. Three further northern spans collapsed on 3 January 2005 as a follow-on stage of the same already-closed crossing. No casualties were reported. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P114, codes vertical erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The watercourse, exact point, municipality attribution and original structural configuration remain under review. No Taloro or Cedrino attribution is made without an identified crossing. No bridge-specific casualties are recorded. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 6 December 2004 – 8 December 2004; the stored date 2004-12-06 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day. The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Ponte Chiavalir over the Vielia at Tramonti di Sopra collapsed at approximately 10:00 on 15 December 2004 during a static load test with three gravel-loaded trucks, before entry into service. The steel deck bent into a V and the vehicles fell into the stream; one driver was injured and nobody died. The testing commission was expected approximately one hour later: this was not an inauguration ceremony. The SR552 / historical SS552 designation and reported 30–35 m span require distinction. Secondary accounts attribute missing bolts and construction irregularities to expert investigations; the final technical and judicial findings should be consulted before a more specific causal assertion. Curator-reviewed structural description: steel longitudinal/transverse members and bracing supporting a concrete slab, coded Steel-concrete composite on the curator’s interpretation. This is a curator-supplied material classification, not a newly inspected original design. The uncertain 30–35 m length remains outside the current public-data correction scope.

properties.bridge_name: Viadotto di Capo di Ponte – svincolo sud
properties.description: At approximately 17:00 on 27 June 2005 a span of the unfinished SS42 south-junction viaduct at Capo di Ponte failed during static load testing. Lateral deck sliding and vehicle overturning were reported while the sixth of ten planned trucks was being positioned. One person died and four were injured; initial reporting gave three injuries. The structure had not entered service. Beam / prestressed-concrete coding and the definitive underlying design/construction cause remain for technical verification. The ministerial reply transcribed by the curator confirms lateral deck sliding during positioning of the sixth test truck, with one death and four injuries. At the date of that reply both the ANAS and ministerial investigations were still ongoing; the account does not establish a final design-error finding.

The 2010 Comune di Massafra tender identifies Ponte Cernera on former SP41 as the crossing lost in the October 2005 flood. properties.description: During the night of 9–10 February 2009 two masonry spans of the SP28 Panoramica Enna–Casina Bianca near km 0+800 collapsed, removing approximately 40 m of roadway. The road had already been closed because of rockfall risk below Rupe di Cerere. The 35 m three-span continuous reinforced-concrete Ponte di Fossa, approximately 5 m wide, collapsed during the 6 April 2009 earthquake. Engineering reconnaissance documents failure of four reinforced-concrete pile-bent columns above water level, lateral displacement and deck penetration. Extensive pre-existing reinforcement corrosion and thin cover were observed. TC is retained. No casualties are assigned to this bridge; the regional earthquake death toll is not a bridge-collapse casualty count.

properties.bridge_name: Ponte della Via Emilia sul Po
properties.description: A span of Ponte della Via Emilia sul Po, carrying SS9 between Piacenza and San Rocco al Porto, collapsed during the 30 April 2009 flood. The original crossing was a metal truss bridge supported by historic masonry piers and abutments, first constructed in 1908 and reconstructed after wartime destruction, not a reinforced-concrete bridge first built in 1949. Three road users were injured and nobody died. TC is retained. Loss of support and failure of a Gerber support detail were discussed in technical investigations; the precise interaction of hydraulic loading, support movement and structural condition must be distinguished from the later acquittal of ANAS officials.

Two road users were injured and the viaduct was closed. Further supporting-system movement caused collapse of a complete supported span on 28 May, with no additional casualties. The active TC record is dated to the latter stage; the two injuries belong to the earlier stage of the same episode. No instantaneous external trigger is identified. A definitive exclusive design/construction cause is not established. Opening of the road in 2006 does not establish the age of every supporting component. Partial collapse of the historic Ponte della Becca (1912 steel truss bridge, SS617, ~1,080 m) on 17 March 2011: pier 9 suddenly collapsed during a Po river flood due to riverbed scour undermining its foundation, documented since November 2010 as anomalous pier rotation. The bridge was saved by two temporary pile-supported bents built in 45 days; surveys in June 2011 showed the scour hole expanding towards pier 8 (founded only 2 m deep). Il 17/03/2011, durante la piena del Po, crollo' improvvisamente la pila 9 del ponte della Becca (acciaio a traliccio, 1912, ~1.080 m, SS617 Broni-Pavia), 'spazzata via senza lasciarne le macerie'. Analisi tecniche (Ingenio/Studio Calvi): gia' da nov. 2010 anomala rotazione-traslazione della pila per erosione del fondo alveo da turbolenza idraulica, con scalzamento della fondazione; i rilievi del giugno 2011 mostrarono la fossa in ampliamento fino a minacciare la pila 8, fondata a soli 2 m (contro gli 11 m delle altre). Struttura salvata con due appoggi provvisori su pali da 45 m realizzati in 45 giorni. D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', IJDRR, database supplementare S3, record P116 (dec=1, PC, danno alle pile) concorda.

The collapse occurred when a yacht and a river barge, dismoored by the surging Magra flood, were swept by the current against the bridge piers, destroying the central span under their combined weight. The event was the fourth flood to hit Ameglia in three years. Later technical and judicial accounts considered insufficient tendon-grout protection and deterioration; these explanations remain attributed to their respective sources rather than treated as a single definitive cause.

Rapporto ARPA Piemonte 'Evento del 2-3 ottobre 2020' (rev 1.1, 14/10/2020, p. 80): nelle valli Sessera e Mosso i processi principali si svilupparono a carico dei corsi d'acqua principali e dei rii secondari, con tracimazioni ed erosioni spondali diffuse e danni alla viabilità nei comuni di Pray, Coggiola e Crevacuore; la Fig. 77 documenta i danni a Crevacuore sul T. Strona di Postua (zona ex cartiera). Il crollo parziale del ponte non è descritto singolarmente nel rapporto: l'attribuzione del processo (erosione spondale/tracimazione) al manufatto è inferita dal contesto documentato nel comune sul medesimo corso d'acqua — associazione da confermare, quindi evidenza 'Probable'. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 2 October 2020 – 3 October 2020; the stored date 2020-10-02 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P156, codes lateral erosion; embankment erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

Ponte Lenzino collapsed over the Trebbia on 3 October 2020 during the flood episode; TC is retained. April 2026 court reporting attributes the governing pressure to the Carisasca landslide and says the GUP rejected river erosion as the cause and discharged the technicians then accused. Libertà's 6 April account additionally reports that expansion-joint mitigation planned in two projects was not implemented, with its reasons and potential management responsibility still unresolved. This is described as unimplemented mitigation, not an independently established intrinsic construction defect or a final finding against an individual. The flooding context is distinguished from the reported geological mechanism; a decisive hydraulic last blow is not asserted. The full expert report and decision were not inspected here. S3 P157's vertical-erosion/other coding remains credited as the authors' alternative classification and is not overwritten, but it does not replace ARCUS's source-attributed landslide interpretation.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Sesia river connecting Romagnano Sesia and Gattinara (Novara, Piemonte) on 3 October 2020. The bridge had been closed overnight as a precaution, was briefly reopened when conditions appeared to improve, then collapsed at approximately 13:30 — the collapse was broadcast in near-real time during a Facebook live session by the two mayors. One person died in the Sesia river floods nearby, but not directly from this collapse. The event was widely reported nationally. Rapporto ARPA Piemonte 'Evento del 2-3 ottobre 2020' (rev 1.1, 14/10/2020, pp. 69-75): il ponte tra Gattinara e Romagnano crollò il 3 ottobre per il cedimento di una pila; il rapporto inquadra il collasso tra le gravi ripercussioni dell'erosione del fondo alveo sulle opere, in un tratto in cui le passate estrazioni di inerti hanno prodotto un abbassamento del fondo di circa 2 m dagli anni '70 con progressiva riduzione della sezione (Fig. 56); la mappatura Copernicus EMS segnala il ponte sulla SP142 seriamente danneggiato (Fig. 41). Contesto: colmi mai registrati sul Sesia (Borgosesia oltre 4 m sopra il livello di pericolo, portata >3000 mc/s). Nota temporale: il rapporto colloca il crollo nella mattina del 3/10, mentre le cronache lo riprendono alle 13:30-13:45 circa, dopo chiusura precauzionale la sera del 2/10 e riapertura alle 12:30. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P158, codes vertical erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

During the 2-3 October 2020 Arroscia flood, Ponte Manfredi at Vessalico sustained a roadway-surface rupture and damage to its abutments. Contemporary news described the bridge as collapsed, whereas the later Regione Liguria emergency-works schedule specifies restoration of road access and consolidation of the existing bridge. The sources do not establish lane passability or the extent of primary-member deformation. PC is retained by curator decision, not as a newly independently verified technical determination. The inspection or project file is still needed to establish physical damage and passability. This crossing is distinct from the SP 83 bridge at Borghetto d'Arroscia, whose documented collapsed span and interrupted transit support TC. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 2 October 2020 – 3 October 2020; the stored date 2020-10-02 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day. The PC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P159, codes others. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity. The other identification/scope checks remain open.

A large portion of the historic Ponte Romano di Bagnasco collapsed during the October 2020 Tanaro flood, as documented by contemporary reporting and drone footage. The official regional works register describes a partial loss of the historic structure; ARCUS retains TC for loss of the affected crossing/span's functionality, not as a claim that the entire multi-span bridge disappeared. ARPA Piemonte documents overtopping and damage to the upper arches. The exact element-by-element failure sequence is not established by these sources. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P160, codes hydraulic load. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity. Hydraulic load is not synonymous with observed overtopping (S3 overtopping: si).

Total collapse of the Passerella Squarciafichi cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Roia river in Ventimiglia (Imperia, Liguria) on 2-3 October 2020, caused by the extreme flooding of the Roia river during the October 2020 Ponente Ligure flood event. The structure was described as a symbol of the city. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P162 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=0.5): processo = erosione verticale (scour); componenti danneggiate = pile, spalle, rilevato di accesso, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no. Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Gesso stream near Valdieri (Cuneo, Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020, caused by the extreme hydraulic loading during the record-breaking October 2020 flood event in the Cuneo Alps. The bridge between Fornero and Piana di Fornero was damaged during the October 2020 flood. A Regione Piemonte works plan calls for reconstruction of the collapsed bridge; February 2021 TV footage documents pedestrian-only access over temporary fill. ARCUS retains the existing TC classification by curator decision: the available video does not by itself establish deformation of all primary members of a span under the adopted TC/PC definition. The exact crossed watercourse also remains to be verified; Rio Fornero is named in the same works entry, while an earlier bridge document names the Strona stream. D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), supplement S3 record P186, attributes scour, with abutment and deck affected and no overtopping evidence. The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian wooden overpass on via Laurentina near Piazzale Ardigò in Rome (Lazio) on 8 October 2020, caused by a crane truck that accidentally struck the underside of the timber bridge while manoeuvring on the road below, splitting the structure in two. The bridge was unoccupied at the time and no injuries were reported. Roma Capitale coordinated restoration works, with the missing span reinstalled in 2021.

properties.bridge_name: Ponte sul Rio Mollarino, località Serre
properties.description: On 15 October 2020, a portion of the road bridge over the Rio Mollarino in località Serre, Picinisco, collapsed during intense rainfall/flooding; a passing car fell into the stream and its driver survived. Contemporary reports differ on whether the driver was injured, so the event-level injury count is left unknown pending a reliable confirmation. The scientific hydraulic-bridge supplement is cited for lateral bank erosion and approach-embankment damage, but the publicly linked news sources do not independently establish the detailed mechanism or dimensions. ARCUS scope review (15 October 2026): the approach component alone does not establish applicability of the restricted extension. Documented physical embankment collapse and its direct connection to this bridge must be established; erosion, inundation, closure or retaining-wall damage alone are insufficient. The existing TC/PC code is not changed or independently validated. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P164, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

Total collapse (washout) of one of three bridges over the Pianale stream between the hamlets of Camasco and Corte e Costa in Varallo (Vercelli, Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020, during the record-breaking Sesia basin flood. The three bridges were washed away by the flood of the Pianale stream and Nono torrent, in a sector where the ARPA Piemonte event report describes hyperconcentrated flows and debris flows along the entire minor network. The three collapses are documented collectively in the report (see B20.10.14-B20.10.16); structural details are not available. No fatalities attributed to these collapses. Rapporto ARPA Piemonte 'Evento del 2-3 ottobre 2020' (rev 1.1, 14/10/2020, p. 70, Fig. 57b e 58): la piena del Rio Pianale e del T. Nono provoco' l'asportazione di tre ponti sul rio Pianale tra Camasco e la frazione Corte e Costa (comune di Varallo). Il rapporto inquadra i processi sui tributari del medio-basso Sesia come trasporto iperconcentrato (piene con elevato trasporto di fondo) e colate detritiche lungo tutto il reticolato minore, con effetti parossistici proprio sui torrenti Nono e Mastallone (p. 69): l'attribuzione 'Debris flow / solid transport' e' inferita da questo contesto documentato, non dichiarata per il singolo manufatto - evidenza 'Probable'. I tre ponti sono documentati collettivamente nel rapporto; il punto del primo ponte è stato confermato durante la curatela ARCUS pre-release. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 2 October 2020 – 3 October 2020; the stored date 2020-10-02 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day.

Total collapse (complete washout) of the footbridge over the Sesia river at Campertogno (Vercelli, Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020. Bank erosion by the Sesia river, which reached unprecedented levels throughout the basin (5.2 m peak at Campertogno vs a 4.0 m danger threshold), damaged the road to the local campsite and completely removed the footbridge, as documented by the ARPA Piemonte event report. No fatalities attributed to this collapse. Rapporto ARPA Piemonte 'Evento del 2-3 ottobre 2020' (rev 1.1, 14/10/2020, p. 71, Fig. 59): a Campertogno l'erosione di sponda ad opera del Sesia causo' danni alla via di collegamento al campeggio e l'asportazione completa della passerella sul torrente. Meccanismo (erosione spondale) e distruzione completa del manufatto documentati dalla didascalia del rapporto: evidenza 'Documented'. Contesto: colmi mai registrati sul Sesia da monte a valle (a Campertogno colmo 5,2 m alle 03:30 UTC del 3/10 contro livello di pericolo 4,0 m, Tab. 5). Tipologia strutturale e materiale non desumibili dal rapporto; coordinate approssimate (zona campeggio di Campertogno, exact_location FALSE). Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 2 October 2020 – 3 October 2020; the stored date 2020-10-02 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day.

Total collapse (complete washout) of the bridge at loc. Barchi in Ormea (Cuneo, Piemonte) over the Tanaro river on 2-3 October 2020. The bridge, rebuilt after the November 1994 flood, was completely washed away by the Tanaro flood, which exceeded the 2016 historical reference levels in the upper valley (estimated return period >200 years). Documented by the ARPA Piemonte event report. No fatalities attributed to this collapse. Rapporto ARPA Piemonte 'Evento del 2-3 ottobre 2020' (rev 1.1, 14/10/2020, p. 93, Fig. 100): a Ormea, loc. Barchi, il ponte - ricostruito dopo l'alluvione del 1994 - fu completamente asportato dalla piena del Tanaro. Il crollo e la causa idraulica sono quindi documentati da fonte tecnica, ma il meccanismo di dettaglio non e' specificato; per l'alta Val Tanaro il rapporto indica in generale numerosi ponti gravemente danneggiati o abbattuti 'sia per l'erosione delle spalle sia per il sormonto delle acque in piena' (p. 92), senza attribuzione al singolo manufatto: processo ed evidenza restano 'Unspecified'. Contesto idrometrico: a Ponte di Nava e Garessio superati i riferimenti storici del 2016, TR stimato >200 anni (Tab. 6). Coordinate approssimate (concentrico di Ormea, exact_location FALSE). Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 2 October 2020 – 3 October 2020; the stored date 2020-10-02 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day.

Partial collapse of the bridge providing access to the Vallone di Monte Colombo just downstream of San Giacomo di Entracque (Cuneo, Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020: left-bank erosion by the Gesso della Barra torrent, in violent flood, removed the bridge abutment. The valley road was also washed away for stretches of hundreds of metres, isolating the hamlet of San Giacomo. Documented by the ARPA Piemonte event report. No fatalities or injuries reported. Rapporto ARPA Piemonte 'Evento del 2-3 ottobre 2020' (rev 1.1, 14/10/2020, p. 89, Fig. 93a): subito a valle di San Giacomo di Entracque, lungo il Gesso della Barra, un'erosione della sponda sinistra asporto' la spalla del ponte utilizzato per accedere al Vallone di Monte Colombo. Meccanismo (erosione spondale) e componente coinvolta (spalla) esplicitamente documentati: evidenza 'Documented'; crollo parziale (PC). Contesto: violenta attivita' torrentizia lungo il T. Gesso della Barra con asportazione della strada del vallone per tratti di centinaia di metri e isolamento di San Giacomo (p. 89, Fig. 92). Tipologia strutturale e materiale non desumibili; coordinate approssimate (zona San Giacomo di Entracque, exact_location FALSE). Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 2 October 2020 – 3 October 2020; the stored date 2020-10-02 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day.

properties.bridge_name: Ponte della SP 83 per Ubaga e Montecalvo
properties.description: During the 2-3 October 2020 flood, one span of the SP 83 bridge over the Arroscia at km 0+100, connecting Borghetto d'Arroscia with Ubaga and Montecalvo, collapsed. The Province of Imperia emergency report records the interruption of vehicular and pedestrian transit; the Regione Liguria works plan specifies reconstruction of the collapsed span. ARCUS classifies this as TC under its adopted span-and-lane-passability definition. The regional plan calls it 'crollo parziale' in the ordinary sense that only part of the bridge collapsed, not as an ARCUS PC classification. The exact collapse day within 2-3 October, casualties, original structural material and precise hydraulic failure process are not established by these sources. The recorded coordinates are Regione Liguria's intervention point and have not been independently confirmed as the bridge centroid. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 2 October 2020 – 3 October 2020; the stored date 2020-10-02 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day.

On 6 November 2020, the first span or part of the bridge over Pallanzeno's Enel canal gave way while a loaded truck was crossing; the driver was unharmed. The mayor suggested that the previous month's flood may have eroded its supports, but this was a hypothesis, not a demonstrated mechanism. Truck passage is documented; exceptional overload is not. Cause and precise structural material remain under review.

On 22 November 2020 the SS106 bridge over the Neto between Crotone and Strongoli closed during flooding. Before the ANAS inspection, CrotoneNews reported visible cracking and serious structural damage. The subsequent same-day ANAS account reproduced by StrettoWeb reported no particular anomalies and reopening that evening. Both accounts remain cited; the later inspection is not omitted. ARCUS retains PC by explicit curator confirmation on 16 October 2026, referring to the damage reported before that inspection, not to a verified collapse of primary members. Scour and the 230 m length are attributed to D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), S3 P172. Exact damage extent and the difference between the reports remain unresolved.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Iornito stream near Melissa (Crotone, Calabria) in November 2020, triggered by hydraulic phenomena. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P173 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione del rilevato in alveo/golena; componenti danneggiate = spalle, rilevato di accesso, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P173, codes embankment erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The bridge on the connection between Osidda and Bitti collapsed during the 28 November 2020 flood, as reported by the Vigili del Fuoco and Il Fatto Quotidiano. This is the crossing selected by the curator to clarify the previously ambiguous Bitti entry. Its exact point, watercourse, dimensions and affected structural components are not established by those reports. ARCUS retains the existing PC code by curator decision, without inferring technical severity from the word collapsed. The former S3 P175 Riu de Malò identification, 13.6 m length and approach-erosion attributes are not transferred without a demonstrated bridge match; that historical scientific record remains cited as context. The regional flood deaths are not assigned to this bridge and bridge-specific casualty counts are unknown.

Ponte Samone on SP26 over the Panaro suffered a partial failure of pier 2 during the 5–6 December 2020 flood and was closed on 6 December. A contemporary Province engineering determination describes six concrete arches over 122 m and, at the first stage, no evident arch or deck lesions. On 24 December, two arches at the damaged pier collapsed; this is the TC event date recorded here because the affected spans lost their primary load path and no lane was passable. D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani S3 P176 dates the case to 6 December, capturing the precursor pier failure; the two stages must not be conflated. The structure combines concrete arches with older stone-faced piers/foundations. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P176, codes vertical erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

A separate pedestrian bridge near Gosaldo was swept away during the 6 December 2020 flood, alongside the vehicle bridge between i Bitti and Ren. A contemporary Repubblica report distinguishes the footbridge from the bridge carrying the fire-service vehicle. D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani S3 P177 gives the pedestrian record and bank-erosion interpretation. Exact location, span length, material and component sequence need bridge-specific verification; the coordinate is retained from prior curation, not independently confirmed here. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P177, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

properties.bridge_name: Ponte tra i Bitti e Ren
properties.description: The vehicle bridge at the Mis/Val de le Eghe confluence linking i Bitti with Ren collapsed on 6 December 2020 during flooding; a fire-service vehicle fell after its occupants escaped. Contemporary mayoral and firefighter accounts identify this crossing and a second, distinct downstream bridge. The precise centroid, structural material, span length and pier arrangement are not established by the sources checked and remain for technical verification.

On 12 May 2021 the movable deck of the Ponte della Darsena di Pagliari at La Spezia collapsed during a closing manoeuvre; no vehicle or vessel was passing and no injuries were reported. Early reports proposed hydraulic-piston failure, but this was a hypothesis, not an established cause. Accounts of the court-appointed expert report later identified interacting design, construction/fastener and maintenance issues, with the detailed allocation of responsibility contested in legal proceedings. ARCUS therefore does not assign a single verified mechanism pending the full technical report. The bridge opening/closing operation is documented as the occasion of failure, not proof of piston causation.

The access bridge to the Saline di Comacchio collapsed on Saturday 28 August 2021, after municipal technicians inspected it and closed it on Friday 27 August because of visible criticalities. No one was injured. Contemporary accounts establish the crossing and sequence, but do not document the precise failure mechanism or verify the bridge's structural system and material. The earlier attribution to structural deterioration is plausible, not a confirmed engineering finding.

During the night of 2–3 October 2021 a fire affected the Ponte dell'Industria over the Tiber in Rome. The Vigili del Fuoco reported heat damage to some structural elements and collapse of approximately 40 m of the adjacent utility/service walkway. The main vehicular deck did not collapse, although the bridge was closed pending inspection. ARCUS therefore records PC, not total collapse of the road bridge, under its adopted primary-member/traffic-safety definition. The ignition source was under investigation; the available official statement mentions bank vegetation and utilities, not a proven origin in a nearby encampment. No injuries were reported. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 2 October 2021 – 3 October 2021; the stored date 2021-10-02 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day.

On 4 October 2021 the bridge on via Tecci over the Quazzola near Quiliano collapsed during exceptional flooding, isolating two households. Contemporary local reporting describes it as an access bridge for private properties; ARCUS does not infer public ownership from the Municipal road-use category. D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), supplement S3 P190, attributes the damage to scour affecting piers and deck. Exact structural type/material still need bridge-specific technical evidence. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P190, codes vertical erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

The SS187 Ponte San Bartolomeo between Alcamo and Castellammare del Golfo suffered collapse of a span after a pier yielded during exceptional flooding in the night of 10–11 December 2021. ANAS's contemporary statement says only part of the bridge collapsed; the crossing was closed and no travel lane could pass, supporting TC for the affected span under ARCUS's adopted definition, not a claim that the entire 115 m structure disappeared. The 115 m overall length comes from the Regione Siciliana's later replacement-bridge statement. A driver stopped before entering the failed crossing; no injuries were reported. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 10 December 2021 – 11 December 2021; the stored date 2021-12-10 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P191, codes vertical erosion; lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity. Multiple cause flags are retained, with no inferred dominant process.

Ponte Guastacconcio on SP 97 in the municipality of Paglieta collapsed over the Sangro on the morning of 13 February 2022. It had been closed since December 2021 following central-pier settlement and road-deck deformation. A parliamentary question links the prior deterioration to repeated Sangro floods and riverbed lowering; D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), S3 P192, codes vertical erosion/scour. No distinct flood is documented at the instant of final collapse, so the immediate trigger is not assigned. Original bridge type, material, exact construction year and overall length still require an owner or design record; the replacement bridge must not be used as evidence for them. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P192, codes vertical erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

On 24 August 2022 an oversize crane transported by a lorry struck the Via Volturno overpass above Brescia's western ring road. Five primary beams were reported damaged, and the Comune di Brescia later specified demolition and replacement of the impact-damaged beams. The municipality describes severe damage to the existing overpass, not collapse of the whole road deck. ARCUS retains PC by curator decision; it does not assert that five beams fell or that the main deck collapsed. Traffic restrictions and urgent stabilisation followed. No injuries were reported in the cited accounts. The PC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Misa river near Arcevia (Ancona, Marche) on 15 September 2022, triggered by the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Marche region. The bridge was destroyed by the extreme hydraulic forces associated with the Misa river in full spate following exceptional rainfall exceeding 400 mm in a few hours in the Cantiano area. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge on the Paraturo stream near Laino Castello (Cosenza, Calabria) on 17 November 2022, triggered by intense rainfall and consequent hydraulic loading. The structure, built approximately 30 years earlier by the Consorzio di Bonifica del Pollino in reinforced concrete, connected the Calabrian municipality to Rotonda (Basilicata). No fatalities or injuries were reported, but residents were left isolated following the collapse. Piena documentata; meccanismo di dettaglio non ricostruibile dalle fonti disponibili.

On the evening of 25 November 2022 an oversize load on the A10 struck the Cavalcavia di via Vignetta near Varazze, damaging the overpass and forcing closure of the motorway beneath it. The structure was judged irreparable and subsequently demolished in a controlled operation, then replaced by a temporary Bailey crossing. ARCUS retains PC by curator decision for the impact-damaged primary members; the available owner/region account describes damage, not collapse of the entire deck at the moment of impact. No casualties were reported. The identity of the specific via Vignetta overpass and the exact member deformation should be checked against the motorway operator's inspection file. The PC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated.

At about 20:30 on 1 December 2022, the SP 329 crossing between Monteverdi Marittimo and Canneto collapsed and the road became impassable. Contemporary ANSA and Sky reports say failure of a pier was a possible explanation, while investigations of the cause were ongoing; ARCUS does not code pier failure or material deterioration as established facts. No vehicle was crossing and no injuries were reported. Bridge material and structural system remain to be checked against the Province of Pisa's technical file.

Partial collapse of Ponte Termini near Terme Vigliatore (Sicily) on 3 December 2022 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with intense flooding of the Mazzarà stream during an extreme rainfall event. No fatalities or injuries were reported Piena documentata; meccanismo di dettaglio non ricostruibile dalle fonti disponibili.

On the night of 15-16 December 2022, two masonry arches of the historic Ponte Tredici Luci collapsed over the Sosio river between Chiusa Sclafani and Burgio, interrupting the crossing. Regione Siciliana announced a technical inspection to assess the damage; the cited official communications do not establish a cause. No casualties were reported in the cited records. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 15 December 2022 – 16 December 2022; the stored date 2022-12-15 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day.

Total collapse of the Collerenti bridge over the Salinello between Bellante and Sant'Omero on 29 December 2022, initiated by failure of the Bellante-side abutment. Initial inspections considered overload, but court-appointed experts later identified a construction defect as the predominant predisposing factor, with rainfall-related erosion and heavy-vehicle traffic as contributing/accelerating factors. No vehicle was crossing at the instant of failure; no discrete trigger is assigned.

On 18 January 2023 the SP 11 bridge over the Aterno at Molina Aterno first developed central-pier settlement and about 50 cm of roadway depression, then lost the structure around 14:00. The mayor's same-day account attributes the event to flooding and accumulated debris; D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), supplementary S3 P201, codes vertical erosion at this crossing. ARCUS does not infer original structural system or material from replacement works. No casualties were reported in the available case accounts. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P201, codes vertical erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

On the afternoon of 30 January 2023 an excavator carried by an overheight vehicle on the E45 struck the Coldipozzo/Promano overpass in the municipality of Città di Castello. ANAS inspection reported a cracked primary girder; the overpassing municipal road closed and a temporary support was installed. The damaged bridge was demolished later because repair could not restore adequate static safety. ARCUS records PC under its severe-primary-member-damage criterion, not a fall of the complete deck at impact. A later retrospective article gives 31 January rather than the contemporary reports' 30 January; the day should be checked against the ANAS incident file.

At about 18:00 on 3 May 2023, the third span of the Ortiano II viaduct on SS 177 near Longobucco collapsed during high flow in the Trionto. D'Angelo et al. (2025), Section 6.4, report in-situ observations: prior exposure of the shallow foundation at pier 3, flow concentration and foundation erosion, pier rotation and loss of the simply supported span. The viaduct entered service in 2016; it did not collapse shortly after opening. Traffic had reportedly been stopped before collapse and no casualties were reported. The hydraulic paper by D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025) is retained as a separate cross-event source. S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P200, codes vertical erosion. Total collapse of a provincial bridge near San Martino in Argine (Emilia-Romagna) on 17 May 2023 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with extreme flooding of the Idice stream during the 2023 Emilia-Romagna flood event. No fatalities or injuries were reported. D'Angelo et al. (2025), Structure and Infrastructure Engineering, case study con sopralluogo degli autori: rottura dell'argine destro dell'Idice ~700 m a valle del ponte della Motta (breccia >100 m, poco dopo mezzanotte del 16/05/2023) -> aumento della pendenza e della velocita' -> incisione generalizzata dell'alveo a monte stimata in ~4 m -> scalzamento dei corpi arginali; le spalle, immorsate negli argini e su fondazioni superficiali (a differenza delle pile su pali), collassarono trascinando due delle tre campate principali; la terza cadde poco dopo, verosimilmente per scalzamento delle pile residue (dati idrometro ARPAE sul ponte fino al collasso; ponte Gerber del 1958, 5 campate, ~100 m). [Il database Polimi (D'Angelo et al. 2025, S3, record P202, dec=1) classifica invece il processo come: erosione laterale di sponda.] S3 source attribution (curator acceptance, 15 October 2026): D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P202, codes lateral erosion. These source classifications are accepted without requiring repetition in the press; they do not independently validate date, TC/PC or bridge identity.

properties.description: The road bridge on Via dei Crivellari (Via Caduti dei Crivellari), Borgo Rivola (Riolo Terme), was completely destroyed by the Senio flood on the morning of 17 May 2023. The Ente Parchi emergency-works document distinguishes this bridge, used by vehicles to reach Via Crivellari, from the nearby cycle-pedestrian footbridge then under construction. The latter collapsed separately during load testing on 7 September 2023. Sources establish the road bridge's total loss and flood context, but not its structural type, material, detailed physical failure process or exact bridge-centroid coordinate.
