Il Telegrafo's 28 July account reports reinforced-concrete fragments falling onto a passing car, without injuries. ARCUS retains PC by the curator's explicit confirmation on 16 October 2026. Beam bridge / Reinforced concrete remain curator-confirmed attributes from the earlier review. The report establishes impact and falling fragments, but not the exact primary member or extent of deck deformation. No complete-span fall or owner-certified PC determination is inferred. Detailed member-level evidence remains unspecified.

Total collapse of the new cycle-pedestrian footbridge at Borgo Rivola (Riolo Terme) during static load testing in September 2023. The structure failed under the water-tank test load; subsequent technical reporting by the designer discusses design errors and reconstruction. Classified as Design and Construction with Static load test trigger and Overstress process. The hydraulic record reported at the same location is not used to override this distinct load-test event.

On 30 October 2023 the Ponte di Ozzanello over the Sporzana between Terenzo and Fornovo lost part of its structure during the flood and road continuity was interrupted. ANSA and the Emilia-Romagna Legislative Assembly call the structural loss 'partial' relative to the entire bridge; ARCUS retains TC under the adopted span-and-passability definition because the affected span/crossing was impassable and had to be reconstructed. The Assembly records the site as Sivizzano–La Fornace/Ponte di Ozzanello and calls for removal of the bridge remnant. Do not repeat the early ANSA headline's erroneous 'sul Taro' as the crossed stream. Original material, system and detailed mechanism require the owner file.

This record represents the bridge in località La Cartaia, Vaiano. Municipal determination 476 of 20 November 2024 cites emergency report 20 of 6 November 2023 for detachment of lateral spallette after the Bisenzio flood and works restoring road safety and transit. The curator explicitly confirms inclusion as PC on 16 October 2026. This is a curator-assigned classification: the cited determination does not identify the spallette as abutments or primary load-bearing members, and ARCUS does not infer severe primary-member deformation from that word alone. The former unidentified footbridge and its TC code are not transferred to La Cartaia. The stored 2 November is the beginning of the 2–6 November flood-to-report window, not a proven exact damage day. Original structure, material, exact point and casualties remain unknown.

On the evening of 2 November 2023 Ponte Ferrone failed as a couple drove over it during the Tuscany flood. Antonino Madonia and Teresa Perone died after their car was swept downstream. A detailed later account of the prosecution's investigation places the bridge over the Rio di Lamporecchio between via Badalino and via Podere Vitetto in Pistoia province/Lamporecchio territory; one earlier report instead calls it Comune di Vinci. The victims and vehicle were found downstream in Vinci, which must not be confused with the bridge point. The prior 4 November date was a reporting date, not the event date. Original beam/concrete attributes are unverified. Exact bridge-centroid coordinates and the administrative boundary should be checked against an owner/GIS or incident file before a new release; no causal findings from the court investigation are asserted here.

The public-use local crossing had already been damaged in May 2023 and was subject to heavy-vehicle restrictions. Following the curator’s review it is classified PC and reinforced concrete. Intense rainfall preceded the failure, but the available evidence does not establish a unique landslide or hydraulic process. No casualties were reported. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 1 May 2024 – 2 May 2024; the stored date 2024-05-01 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day. The PC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Other evidence limitations remain as stated.

The curator’s reviewed classification confirms TC, a reinforced-concrete beam bridge and the event point. The specific hydraulic failure process remains unconfirmed. No bridge-specific casualties are recorded. The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. TC and zero casualties are retained; the smaller Via Petrarca bridge remains a separate candidate. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 15 May 2024 – 16 May 2024; the stored date 2024-05-15 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day. The curator confirms this bridge’s location, steel beam structure and timber deck surface; Steel identifies the principal load-bearing material, not the timber surfacing. TC is supported by the loss of multiple spans. The exact day within 29–30 June is unresolved; the stored 29 June is the conventional interval start. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 29 June 2024 – 30 June 2024; the stored date 2024-06-29 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day. On 5 September 2024 the Rio Gerardo flood washed away the municipal bridge serving upper borgata Giordani at Mattie. Regione Piemonte documents before-and-after views in figure 13, PDF p.18 (printed p.16). The curator confirms the matching point and the original reinforced-concrete beam structure. This is distinct from the nearby SP207 bridge and the Combe crossing. TC is supported by the lost deck; a specific boulder-impact diagnosis is not asserted.

The stored 18 October is the conventional start of that interval, not a confirmed exact failure day. Subsequent Army removal of the failed superstructure and an emergency bypass are not the original natural collapse. TC is retained by curator decision. The original Arch bridge/Masonry attribution and the detailed hydraulic process remain for documentary confirmation. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 18 October 2024 – 19 October 2024; the stored date 2024-10-18 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day. The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. The SP167/3 road bridge over the Cottola collapsed during the 20–21 October 2024 flood in the Maida / San Pietro a Maida area. The April 2025 executive design describes the original bridge as three masonry arches built mainly of local stone, approximately 40.70 m long, with direct foundations compromised by erosion and flood action. Total destruction is explicitly documented. Construction is estimated by the designers to 1945–1950; no exact construction year is assigned. No casualties were reported in contemporary accounts. The reinforced/prestressed-concrete beam bridge described elsewhere in the project is the replacement, not the failed original. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 20 October 2024 – 21 October 2024; the stored date 2024-10-20 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day.

Contemporary accounts identify the crossing and describe it as broken in two. TC, Beam bridge and Reinforced concrete are retained following the curator’s personal review in Punti da verificare.xlsx, Foglio2!G89. The material classification is curator-supplied, not independently established here from railings or supports. The curator’s replacement point is used at site-level precision and is not the earlier Via Roma OSM bridge match. Later demolition/reconstruction is separate from the flood damage. Date convention (curator, 15 October 2026): documented event window 26 October 2024 – 27 October 2024; the stored date 2024-10-26 is its first day, not a confirmed exact failure day. The TC classification is retained by curator decision of 15 October 2026; the TC/PC coding question is closed without claiming new independent technical validation. Total collapse of Ponte Gilino, a municipal bridge near Mongrando (Piedmont), on 17 April 2025 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with intense rainfall and flooding of the Elvo stream.
